intro: Reporting builds research, deadline discipline and the ability to explain complex events. The closest of the 25 careers below is Producers and Directors, with an 85% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $90,360, which is 45% more than the $62,200 news analysts, reporters and journalists earn.
why_it_works: A news day means finding sources, checking facts, writing clearly and filing on time. O*NET rates social perceptiveness at 3.75 out of 5 for this job and time management at 3.62. Producing, video editing, public relations and intelligence analysis use those skills. Most matches need no new degree. The common gaps are business skills: budgets, managing resources and analyzing operations.
tips: Build a portfolio that groups your best work by skill: investigation, data stories, video or editing.
Public relations is the best-paid path here: PR managers earn $146,910, which is 136% more.
Film and Video Editors earn $75,420, or 21% more, if you already shoot or cut video.

faq.q: What jobs can former journalists do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Producers and Directors (85%), Film and Video Editors (78%) and Media Programming Directors (75%), based on O*NET 31.0. Proofreaders and Copy Markers are 72% matched but earn $51,120, which is 18% less than the $62,200 median for news analysts, reporters and journalists.

faq.q: Which careers for journalists pay more?
faq.a: 16 of the 25 matches pay more than reporting. Public Relations Managers earn $146,910 (136% more), Political Scientists $142,080 (128% more) and Advertising and Promotions Managers $133,660 (115% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Political science usually requires a graduate degree.

faq.q: Do journalists need another degree to change careers?
faq.a: Usually not. 23 of the 25 matches need no more education than journalists already have, and only 2 usually need a graduate degree. A bachelor's degree is common, held by 57% of workers in the closest match, so your clips matter most.

The skills that most often need work are operations analysis, managing materials, managing financial resources and systems evaluation. Complex problem solving already rates 3.38 out of 5 for journalists in O*NET, so budgets and business planning are the main gaps for producer and manager jobs.
